subject: [URGENT] We're being rate-limited — production down on our side
body:
Priya — our production traffic to Northwind is being rejected at high rate as of ~17:14 UTC. SLA-impacting. We have an eng-side incident open. What's going on?

Brent

subject: Re: [URGENT] We're being rate-limited — production down on our side
body:
Brent — confirmed, this is on us. Initial diagnosis: your rate limit wasn't updated to reflect your Q1 expansion, so legitimate traffic is being capped at the old ceiling. Our platform team is mitigating now — Rohan (cc'd) is on the bridge.

ETA to mitigation: minutes, not hours. I'll send a fuller update by 18:00 UTC and we'll send a formal incident notice + SLA credit memo by EOD tomorrow.

Rohan or I will pick up your phone if useful — DM me the right number.

Priya

subject: Hooli — what do I tell them, what's the timeline?
body:
Rohan, Mei — Brent (Hooli VPE) just escalated. They have an eng-side incident open. I need to give them ETA and root-cause framing within 15 min.

What can I say truthfully right now? Specifically:
- Is it a config issue or a system issue?
- Are other tenants affected?
- Mitigation ETA?

Will follow your lead on what's safe to share.

P

subject: Re: Hooli — what do I tell them, what's the timeline?
body:
Confirmed: config issue compounded by a design gap.

- Their tenant rate limit was set at onboarding 2023, not adjusted for their Q1 2025 expansion. So they hit a ceiling that no longer matches what they bought. That's the config issue.
- Our gateway has a global circuit breaker that trips when one tenant produces > 30% of all 429s. Hooli tripped it. So briefly other tenants saw degradation. That's the design gap.

Safe to tell them:
- It's our config, not their traffic.
- Mitigation: we've raised their limit to expansion-correct as of 17:30. Traffic recovering.
- Other tenants briefly affected, isolated quickly.
- We'll write a postmortem and send SLA credit. Expected by EOW.

Not to share publicly: the global circuit breaker behavior is a known design gap; we'll mention 'cascade isolation' in the postmortem at appropriate detail.

—r

subject: Re: [URGENT] We're being rate-limited — incident update 18:00 UTC
body:
Brent —

Update. Service recovering as of 17:30 UTC, fully clean by 17:52.

What happened: your tenant rate limit wasn't adjusted when you expanded in Q1, so legitimate traffic was being throttled at the old ceiling. That's our config gap, not your traffic. Limit is now correct.

A briefer secondary effect: our global circuit breaker briefly affected a small percentage of traffic on other tenants during the 38-min window. Isolated.

What we owe you:
- Formal incident notice + postmortem: by EOW (May 30).
- SLA credit memo: by Tuesday May 27.
- Process fix: automation linking contract changes to limit config — we have a plan for this and I'll share scope on the postmortem.

Apologies. If your incident review needs Rohan on a call, we're available.

Priya

subject: Re: [URGENT] We're being rate-limited — appreciate the directness
body:
Priya — appreciate the directness yesterday. Honest framing made our internal review much easier.

Looking forward to the postmortem. Don't bother with the SLA credit if it's small — I'd rather have the engineering investment go into the automation fix you mentioned than a check.

Brent

subject: Hooli — would you be open to being a reference?
body:
Hi Brent,

Incident postmortem went out last week. Action items are tracking — the contract-change-to-limit automation is in flight for Q3.

Different ask: would Hooli be open to being a reference for us? The way your team handled the incident — direct, focused on engineering fix over commercial concession — is exactly the partnership we'd want prospects to know is possible. Happy to scope what 'reference' means to your comfort level.

No rush, no pressure.

Best,
Priya

subject: Re: Hooli — would you be open to being a reference?
body:
Yes. Let's do a written reference quote first, see how a prospect call goes after. Send me the draft quote, I'll edit.

Brent
